passages.text: How the gold has become tarnished, the pure gold has become dull! The gems of the temple lie scattered on every street corner.
passages.sermon:
Gold was once bright and valuable.
Now the gold is tarnished.
Pure gold was once shining and precious.
Now the pure gold is dull.
The temple had holy gems.
Now the holy gems lie scattered.
They are on every street corner.
passages.original: אֵיכָה֙ יוּעַ֣ם זָהָ֔ב יִשְׁנֶ֖א הַכֶּ֣תֶם הַטּ֑וֹב תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֙כְנָה֙ אַבְנֵי־ קֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּרֹ֖אשׁ כָּל־ חוּצֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: How the precious sons of Zion, once worth their weight in pure gold, are now esteemed as jars of clay, the work of a potter’s hands!
passages.sermon:
The sons of Zion were precious.
They were highly valued.
People compared them to pure gold.
Now people see them as jars of clay.
A potter makes jars of clay with his hands.
People no longer honor the sons of Zion.
People treat them as common and fragile.
They are no longer seen as valuable.
passages.original: בְּנֵ֤י צִיּוֹן֙ הַיְקָרִ֔ים הַמְסֻלָּאִ֖ים בַּפָּ֑ז אֵיכָ֤ה נֶחְשְׁבוּ֙ לְנִבְלֵי־ חֶ֔רֶשׂ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יְדֵ֥י יוֹצֵֽר׃ס

passages.text: Even jackals offer their breasts to nurse their young, but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like an ostrich in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
Jackals are wild animals.
Jackals care for their young.
Jackals offer their breasts to nurse their young.
The daughter of my people is different.
She has become cruel.
She does not care for her children.
She is like an ostrich in the wilderness.
Ostriches in the wilderness are known for their lack of care for their young.
passages.original: גַּם־ תַּנִּין חָ֣לְצוּ שַׁ֔ד הֵינִ֖יקוּ גּוּרֵיהֶ֑ן בַּת־ עַמִּ֣י לְאַכְזָ֔ר כִּי עֵנִים בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃ס

passages.text: The nursing infant’s tongue clings in thirst to the roof of his mouth. Little children beg for bread, but no one gives them any.
passages.sermon:
A nursing infant feels great thirst.
His tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth.
Little children ask for bread.
No one gives them bread.
passages.original: דָּבַ֨ק לְשׁ֥וֹן יוֹנֵ֛ק אֶל־ חכּ֖וֹ בַּצָּמָ֑א עֽוֹלָלִים֙ שָׁ֣אֲלוּ לֶ֔חֶם פֹּרֵ֖שׂ אֵ֥ין לָהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Those who once ate delicacies are destitute in the streets; those brought up in crimson huddle in ash heaps.
passages.sermon:
Some people once ate fine foods.
These people now have nothing.
They are destitute in the streets.
Some people grew up wearing rich, crimson clothes.
These people now huddle in ash heaps.
passages.original: הָאֹֽכְלִים֙ לְמַ֣עֲדַנִּ֔ים נָשַׁ֖מּוּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת הָאֱמֻנִים֙ עֲלֵ֣י תוֹלָ֔ע חִבְּק֖וּ אַשְׁפַּתּֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: The punishment of the daughter of my people is greater than that of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant without a hand turned to help her.
passages.sermon:
The daughter of my people has received great punishment.
Her punishment is greater than the punishment of Sodom.
God destroyed Sodom in a single moment.
No one tried to help Sodom when it was destroyed.
passages.original: וַיִּגְדַּל֙ עֲוֺ֣ן בַּת־ עַמִּ֔י מֵֽחַטַּ֖את סְדֹ֑ם הַֽהֲפוּכָ֣ה כְמוֹ־ רָ֔גַע וְלֹא־ חָ֥לוּ בָ֖הּ יָדָֽיִם׃ס

passages.text: Her dignitaries were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were more ruddy than rubies, their appearance like sapphires.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem once had dignitaries.
These dignitaries were very important and respected.
Their appearance was brighter than snow.
Their skin was whiter than milk.
Their bodies were more red than rubies.
Their form looked like sapphires.
passages.original: זַכּ֤וּ נְזִירֶ֙יהָ֙ מִשֶּׁ֔לֶג צַח֖וּ מֵחָלָ֑ב אָ֤דְמוּ עֶ֙צֶם֙ מִפְּנִינִ֔ים סַפִּ֖יר גִּזְרָתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: But now their appearance is blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become as dry as a stick.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem once had dignitaries who looked bright and healthy.
Now their appearance is blacker than soot.
People do not recognize them in the streets.
Their skin has shriveled on their bones.
Their skin has become as dry as a stick.
passages.original: חָשַׁ֤ךְ מִשְּׁחוֹר֙ תָּֽאֳרָ֔ם לֹ֥א נִכְּר֖וּ בַּחוּצ֑וֹת צָפַ֤ד עוֹרָם֙ עַל־ עַצְמָ֔ם יָבֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֥ה כָעֵֽץ׃ס

passages.text: Those slain by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger, who waste away, pierced with pain because the fields lack produce.
passages.sermon:
People died in Jerusalem.
Some people died by the sword.
Others died from hunger.
Those killed by the sword suffered less.
Those who died from hunger suffered more.
The hungry wasted away.
They felt pain like being pierced.
The fields had no food.
The lack of produce caused their suffering.
passages.original: טוֹבִ֤ים הָיוּ֙ חַלְלֵי־ חֶ֔רֶב מֵֽחַלְלֵ֖י רָעָ֑ב שֶׁ֣הֵ֤ם יָז֙וּבוּ֙ מְדֻקָּרִ֔ים מִתְּנוּבֹ֖ת שָׂדָֽי׃ס

passages.text: The hands of compassionate women have cooked their own children, who became their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
passages.sermon:
Compassionate women acted.
These women used their own hands.
They cooked their own children.
Their children became food for them.
This happened during the destruction of the daughter of my people.
passages.original: יְדֵ֗י נָשִׁים֙ רַחֲמָ֣נִיּ֔וֹת בִּשְּׁל֖וּ יַלְדֵיהֶ֑ן הָי֤וּ לְבָרוֹת֙ לָ֔מוֹ בְּשֶׁ֖בֶר בַּת־ עַמִּֽי׃ס

passages.text: The LORD has exhausted His wrath; He has poured out His fierce anger; He has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has consumed her foundations.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD became very angry.
The LORD finished His wrath.
The LORD poured out His fierce anger.
The LORD started a fire in Zion.
The fire burned the foundations of Zion.
The fire destroyed the base of the city.
passages.original: כִּלָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ חֲמָת֔וֹ שָׁפַ֖ךְ חֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ וַיַּצֶּת־ אֵ֣שׁ בְּצִיּ֔וֹן וַתֹּ֖אכַל יְסוֹדֹתֶֽיהָ׃ס

passages.text: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor any people of the world, that an enemy or a foe could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The kings ruled over all the earth.
All the people lived in the world.
None of them believed this could happen.
They did not believe an enemy could enter Jerusalem.
They did not believe a foe could come through her gates.
passages.original: לֹ֤א הֶאֱמִ֙ינוּ֙ מַלְכֵי־ אֶ֔רֶץ וְכֹל יֹשְׁבֵ֣י תֵבֵ֑ל כִּ֤י יָבֹא֙ צַ֣ר וְאוֹיֵ֔ב בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֖י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: But this was for the sins of her prophets and the guilt of her priests, who shed the blood of the righteous in her midst.
passages.sermon:
The prophets in Jerusalem sinned.
The priests in Jerusalem became guilty.
These prophets and priests lived among the people.
They shed the blood of righteous people in Jerusalem.
God punished Jerusalem because of these sins and this guilt.
passages.original: מֵֽחַטֹּ֣את נְבִיאֶ֔יהָ עֲוֺנ֖וֹת כֹּהֲנֶ֑יהָ הַשֹּׁפְכִ֥ים בְּקִרְבָּ֖הּ דַּ֥ם צַדִּיקִֽים׃ס

passages.text: They wandered blind in the streets, defiled by this blood, so that no one dared to touch their garments.
passages.sermon: Blind people wandered in the streets.\r\nBlood defiled them.\r\nNo one dared to touch their clothes.
passages.original: נָע֤וּ עִוְרִים֙ בַּֽחוּצ֔וֹת נְגֹֽאֲל֖וּ בַּדָּ֑ם בְּלֹ֣א יֽוּכְל֔וּ יִגְּע֖וּ בִּלְבֻשֵׁיהֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: “Go away! Unclean!” men shouted at them. “Away, away! Do not touch us!” So they fled and wandered. Among the nations it was said, “They can stay here no longer.”
passages.sermon:
The people saw the prophets and priests.
The prophets and priests had sinned.
The prophets and priests had shed the blood of the righteous.
People shouted at them, “Go away! You are unclean!”
People said, “Go away! Go away! Do not touch us!”
The prophets and priests ran away.
They wandered from place to place.
Other nations saw them.
The nations said, “They cannot stay here any longer.”
passages.original: ס֣וּרוּ טָמֵ֞א קָ֣רְאוּ לָ֗מוֹ ס֤וּרוּ ס֙וּרוּ֙ אַל־ תִּגָּ֔עוּ כִּ֥י נָצ֖וּ גַּם־ נָ֑עוּ אָֽמְרוּ֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יפוּ לָגֽוּר׃ס

passages.text: The presence of the LORD has scattered them; He regards them no more. The priests are shown no honor; the elders find no favor.
passages.sermon:
The LORD turned away from them.
He scattered them.
He does not look at them anymore.
People do not honor the priests.
People do not show favor to the elders.
passages.original: פְּנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ חִלְּקָ֔ם לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַבִּיטָ֑ם פְּנֵ֤י כֹהֲנִים֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔אוּ זְקֵנִים לֹ֥א חָנָֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: All the while our eyes were failing as we looked in vain for help. We watched from our towers for a nation that could not save us.
passages.sermon:
The people of Jerusalem suffered.
They looked for help.
Their eyes grew weak from waiting.
They hoped for rescue.
They watched and waited for another nation.
That nation could not save them.
Their hope was in vain.
passages.original: עוֹדֵינָה תִּכְלֶ֣ינָה עֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֶל־ עֶזְרָתֵ֖נוּ הָ֑בֶל בְּצִפִּיָּתֵ֣נוּ צִפִּ֔ינוּ אֶל־ גּ֖וֹי לֹ֥א יוֹשִֽׁעַ׃ס

passages.text: They stalked our every step, so that we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near, our time ran out, for our end had come!
passages.sermon:
Our enemies stalked us.
They watched every step we took.
We could not walk in our own streets.
Our end came close.
Our days were finished.
Our end arrived.
passages.original: צָד֣וּ צְעָדֵ֔ינוּ מִלֶּ֖כֶת בִּרְחֹבֹתֵ֑ינוּ קָרַ֥ב קִצֵּ֛ינוּ מָלְא֥וּ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כִּי־ בָ֥א קִצֵּֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: Those who chased us were swifter than the eagles in the sky; they pursued us over the mountains and ambushed us in the wilderness.
passages.sermon:
Our enemies chased us.
They moved faster than eagles in the sky.
They followed us over the mountains.
They set ambushes for us in the wilderness.
passages.original: קַלִּ֤ים הָיוּ֙ רֹדְפֵ֔ינוּ מִנִּשְׁרֵ֖י שָׁמָ֑יִם עַל־ הֶהָרִ֣ים דְּלָקֻ֔נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר אָ֥רְבוּ לָֽנוּ׃ס

passages.text: The LORD’s anointed, the breath of our life, was captured in their pits. We had said of him, “Under his shadow we will live among the nations.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD chose a special person.
This person is the LORD’s anointed.
He gave us life and hope.
He was like the breath in our bodies.
Our enemies trapped him.
They captured him in their pits.
We had trusted him.
We said, “We will live safely under his protection.”
We believed we could live among the nations because of him.
passages.original: ר֤וּחַ אַפֵּ֙ינוּ֙ מְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה נִלְכַּ֖ד בִּשְׁחִיתוֹתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְנוּ בְּצִלּ֖וֹ נִֽחְיֶ֥ה בַגּוֹיִֽם׃ס

passages.text: So rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz. Yet the cup will pass to you as well; you will get drunk and expose yourself.
passages.sermon:
Daughter of Edom, you live in the land of Uz.
You rejoice now.
You are glad now.
But the cup of judgment will come to you also.
You will drink from it.
You will become drunk.
You will expose yourself in shame.
passages.original: שִׂ֤ישִׂי וְשִׂמְחִי֙ בַּת־ אֱד֔וֹם יוֹשַׁבְתִּי בְּאֶ֣רֶץ ע֑וּץ גַּם־ עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ תַּעֲבָר־ כּ֔וֹס תִּשְׁכְּרִ֖י וְתִתְעָרִֽי׃ס

passages.text: O Daughter of Zion, your punishment is complete; He will not prolong your exile. But He will punish your iniquity, O Daughter of Edom; He will expose your sins.
passages.sermon:
Daughter of Zion, you are the people of Jerusalem.
Your punishment is now finished.
God will not send you into exile again.
Daughter of Edom, you are the people of Edom.
God will punish your sins.
He will reveal your wrongdoing.
passages.original: תַּם־ עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־ צִיּ֔וֹן לֹ֥א יוֹסִ֖יף לְהַגְלוֹתֵ֑ךְ פָּקַ֤ד עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ בַּת־ אֱד֔וֹם גִּלָּ֖ה עַל־ חַטֹּאתָֽיִךְ׃פ
